Killer breast feeding hormone

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Young mothers are dying in South Africa from a completely preventable heart condition brought on by breast feeding. 1 in 1000 mothers contract this fatal heart condition and 25% of those die from it within the first few years of giving birth. Tragically its completely treatable with a very inexpensive drug. They're dying because they go undiagnosed until its too late because their symptoms are similar to so many other associated with the early post-partum ailments. These are healthy young women who had perfect pregnancies- there were no warning signs until after the birth.
It effects women of all races.


Summary:
Heart disease is on the increase in South Africa and alarmingly it’s affecting more young people. One of the heart conditions that often goes un-detected until it’s too late is Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM). It is a global phenomenon but in parts of Africa like in Nigeria it affects one in 300 new mothers.

The rate of PPCM could be in fact be far higher than currently documented because maternal deaths are only recorded up to 6 months after a woman has given birth. Women can die within 12-24 months after the birth and so do not fall into the maternal mortality figures.
PPCM is caused by a defect in the hormone prolactin which is responsible for milk production. The women are fine during their pregnancy and then weeks sometimes months after the birth they begin to experience extreme fatigue, a shortness of breath, their legs and face swell. All these ailments are often associated with the exhaustion of raising a young infant and so go un-diagnosed.
Groote Schuur has a specialised Cardiac Maternal clinic where these women can be treated but most hospitals don’t and many of these women are treated at clinic and often misdiagnosed as having asthma rather than a chronic heart condition. One of the major problems of late diagnosis is that the damage to the heart has already been done and although the mother may get help she may only live for a few years leaving very young children. Some woman have had to have a leg amputated below the knee due to poor circulation and their life prospects are very poor.
The treatment is quite simple and cheap and if the condition is picked up quickly woman recover well. If they have another pregnancy they can take a pill immediately after the birth and do not breast feed to prevent the condition developing. Some women have no problems with the first birth and the condition only presents after the second child.




Further information:
In September 2018 the Would Health organization adopted the treatment into the International Guidelines, this generic medication and extremely cheap. This is a major success for UCT's Prof Karen Silwa who has been part of this 20 year study

Shaheema Chinian was 28 years old and had a healthy 3 year old when she gave birth to her second child. She was extremely tired after her 2nd baby and she and her mother put it down to looking after two very small children. Within two months after the birth her face began to swell and she was short of breath. The local clinic treated her for asthma, but her condition did not improve. She returned to the clinic several times before going to Groote Schuur. Then suddenly her face and tongue swelled and her mother insisted she return to Groote Schuur. It took several visits before she finally told her mother that she had a heart condition. Sadly Shaheema died when her baby was just 4 months old and her first born only 3 years old. She was in her final year of law at UWC. Her death was completely preventable. Shaheema's parent are willing to be interviewed.

The latest being a nursing sister who despite her medical knowledge had ver heard of this condition and she too just thought it was a result of being the mother of 3 small children. her first two pregnancies were fine.

Press Release:


Rogue Hormone Meets its Match
It’s a baffling and avoidable heart condition that until now has gone mostly undiagnosed because it’s detected too late. Peripartum cardiomyopathy, triggered by a hormone that’s released when breastfeeding starts, affects as many as one in a thousand young mothers and 25% of them will die – unnecessarily. Carte Blanche tells the story of pioneering medical research by Groote Schuur doctors who have discovered a simple and inexpensive treatment.
Producer: Liz Fish
Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


Sorayda: “I never suspected anything that she could do that she could die because she was healthy and she attended the clinics and I really don't know what went wrong there.”
Zintle: “I'm very hyper active. Talkative I walk very fast. Whatever I do all I do know is if I'm in a rush. But when I was diagnosed with this illness everything of mine was like in slow motion.”
Phumeza: “The way I was so weak I couldn't take care of her my sister was there to take care of her. I couldn't even pick it up. I was just looking at it thinking myself oh you are the one who gave me all this”
Link: Breast feeding is one of the most fundamental bonds between mother and child, it is a deeply primal act, but what if that very act, kills the mother?
Script: For centuries, young mothers have been dying from a mysterious heart disease unique to pregnancy, known as peripartum cardiomyopathy. Professor Karen Sliwa first encountered it as a young mother
Karen: The lady looking after my two young daughters sadly had a stillbirth, and three months afterwards she actually developed a peripartum cardiomyopathy and heart failure. So that's where when I later became a trainee in cardiology I decided that would be a very important area to do research.
Script: And for the next 20 years she dedicated her life to finding the cause.
Link “The research around this fatal condition has been part of an International study, driven by the Hatter institute at UCT’s medical school
Script: With Professor Sliwa at the helm.
Karen: “We are understanding now that some women produce an abnormal breast feeding hormone so instead of the normal hormone leading to lactation they produce a different one which can damage the heart. So the women are totally healthy and fine, but at the end of the pregnancy or after delivery the heart is giving up.
Script: The aberrant breastfeeding hormone closes down the very small vessels in the heart, and without sufficient blood, eventually the heart muscle can’t pump.
Karen: “So instead of pumping like that. It stops pumping only very little and then because of the blood which comes into the heart it can't be pushed out it gets stuck in the legs and gets stuck in the lung and that's what we call heart failure
Link “This heart condition is a killer because so few people know about it, and scarily the women are young and have no history of heart disease.
Script: Avuyile was Zintle’s Rani first baby, arriving in February this year to a fit and healthy mom.
Zintle “When the baby was born he was healthy, I was okay as well as excited, he just brought joy into my life
Link: Every woman who has had a child knows how incredibly exciting, yet physically exhausting it is, to be a new mom. So when Zintle felt tired she accepted it as a normal part of motherhood - little did she know that those were the early signs of her heart failing
Zintle: “First phase after giving birth obviously you must wake up every two hours to breastfeed. I thought it's new to me, motherhood. In May month things got a bit hectic whereby I couldn't carry him. He felt so heavy I was coughing I thought it's TB at first
Script: Head of Cardiology at Groote Schuur hospital Professor Mpiko Ntsekhe, says the early signs can be mild and easily dismissed, but as the illness develops
Ntsekhe “It causes people to be short of breath. They can be very tired. Their ability to do a lot of things that they're used to doing is often impaired.
Script: Zintle went to her private GP who diagnosed her with bronchitis, she felt stronger so returned to work at the end of her maternity leave.
Zintle: I kind of forced myself I tried to push and went to work because I've got a baby. My mom is a pensioner my sister's not working. So I try to push and go to work even though I could feel that my body couldn't take it anymore
Script: Then she landed in hospital unable to breathe, four months after Avuyile was born, she was diagnosed with severe PPCM
Claire “That must have come as huge shock?
Zintle: It was a shock, I was in denial. That is why I would push myself and tell myself that no man, there's no such thing. I've got no heart condition. Where does it come from? And realize by getting more ill, this is a reality, this is real
Script: PPCM struck Phumeza Hanise only after her third child Lea. The pregnancy and birth had gone well, but those first few days after she was discharged, were hell.
Phumeza: I couldn't even dress me. I couldn't even put a tight or a pantie on me I couldn't even do nothing the way I was tired if I bend be so difficult for me to get up again. I was very scared because I thought I don’t want to die and leave my baby because this tiredness it really going to take me to grave the way I was.
Link: “Shaheema was 28 years old had just had her 2nd child and was studying part time, her life was full of promise
Sorayda: She was a bubbly person. Wherever she goes she makes everything alive. She was a good daughter to me.
Script: Shaheema was Sorayda Latief’s only child. She had waited 9 years for her, and was delighted, when Shaheema gave her two grandchildren
Sorayda: The second one was two weeks old. Then one morning she just woke up and was swollen all on the face. I took it to the private doctor, and then he said its asthma. So after the week it got worse, everything was swollen and she was a tiny person.
Karen: For almost everybody it just comes out of the blue. Because we only know fairly recently how common it is how severe it can be and how to treat it. It's not yet taught everywhere at medical schools not only in South Africa but also globally because it's relatively new knowledge
Prof Mpiko Ntsekhe “If left untreated, most people will go into intractable heart failure.
Script: Sadly, by the time Shaheema got to Groote Schuur, the damage to her heart was already done.
Sorayda “She said I am too tired Mommy. I can’t be a Mommy for them. But you are strong and you must look after them. I said I'm going to take you to hospital and you can come back home. She said ok its fine
Script: She never did, Yugyah was only 4 months old, and Ifa was 3 when she died. She was going to be a lawyer and had got her first job. It’s been a huge struggle for Sorayda who has suffered two heart attacks since her daughter’s death.
Claire: “Are there anything symptoms that a new mother should be worrying about
Karen: I think every woman that is pregnant or just baby and become short of breath should actually really immediately go to a clinic.
Link “One in one thousand women contract PPCM, and a quarter of them die within the first year of their child’s birth. But the numbers could be higher, because if they die 2 months after their child is born, it’s not even recorded as a maternal death
Script: But breast is still best, avoiding breast feeding won’t prevent the onset of this heart disease, because the hormone is already peaking in the pregnant body and for the first five months after birth.
Claire: “We're not telling people not to breastfeed.
Prof. Mpiko Ntsekhe “Oh I think that must be a hundred percent clear. We are certainly not and the health benefits both for mother ironically and baby of breastfeeding should never be underestimated and certainly we would not want to get any form of message that says don't breastfeed
Script: Over a cup of coffee with a Swiss colleague who was studying mice with weak heart muscles, Professor Sliwa made a major scientific breakthrough
Karen ” Drinking coffee and coffee and thinking and thinking and then we thought perhaps it must be a hormone. So then she measured actually in the mice that hormone and realized that this is an abnormal breast feeding hormone. And then I measured it in the blood of the women, and then at the same abnormal hormone.
Script: And that was the beginning of a global study across 53 countries, the clinical research trial in Germany confirmed that if they could stop the lactating, they could save the heart
Link: “This ordinary looking pill is the difference between of life and death for the mothers who suffer from this peculiar disease. It’s the difference between seeing their children grow up, or not., Bromocriptine is just R20 for a course and is available worldwide
Karen “And you only have to take it if you have a milder form of the disease for a week and if you have a more severe form for six weeks.
Prof. Mpiko Ntsekhe “ What we know about Peripartum cardiomyopathy is that relative to all forms of heart muscle disease and heart failure, it's actually one that most people believe carries with it the best prognosis
Script: Phumeza was diagnosed within a month of Lia’s birth, and has been on treatment now for 18 months.
Karen: ” If you look her you can see your heart is beating much better contracting,
Link “Phumeza has come in to check how well her heart is beating and the good news is that she is recovering well on the medication.
Phumeza: “I don't get tired anymore I can work fine
Zintle: “I would call my best day is if I'm able to wake up and make my own bed. I have been told my heart is beating on twelve percent instead of 50. I have been listed for heart transplant because my heart is weak.
Claire: So the idea of a heart transplant is hectic.
Zintle “I want to be saved. And I said I want to see my baby grow
Script: Professor Sliwa still hopes they will find a way to prevent PPCM, but for now she hopes awareness will save more women’s lives.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Young mothers are dying in South Africa from a completely preventable heart condition brought on by breast feeding. 1 in 1000 mothers contract this fatal heart condition and 25% of those die from it within the first few years of giving birth. Tragically its completely treatable with a very inexpensive drug. They're dying because they go undiagnosed until its too late because their symptoms are similar to so many other associated with the early post-partum ailments. These are healthy young women who had perfect pregnancies- there were no warning signs until after the birth. It effects women of all races.
metadata.Summary: Heart disease is on the increase in South Africa and alarmingly it’s affecting more young people. One of the heart conditions that often goes un-detected until it’s too late is Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM). It is a global phenomenon but in parts of Africa like in Nigeria it affects one in 300 new mothers. The rate of PPCM could be in fact be far higher than currently documented because maternal deaths are only recorded up to 6 months after a woman has given birth. Women can die within 12-24 months after the birth and so do not fall into the maternal mortality figures. PPCM is caused by a defect in the hormone prolactin which is responsible for milk production. The women are fine during their pregnancy and then weeks sometimes months after the birth they begin to experience extreme fatigue, a shortness of breath, their legs and face swell. All these ailments are often associated with the exhaustion of raising a young infant and so go un-diagnosed. Groote Schuur has a specialised Cardiac Maternal clinic where these women can be treated but most hospitals don’t and many of these women are treated at clinic and often misdiagnosed as having asthma rather than a chronic heart condition. One of the major problems of late diagnosis is that the damage to the heart has already been done and although the mother may get help she may only live for a few years leaving very young children. Some woman have had to have a leg amputated below the knee due to poor circulation and their life prospects are very poor. The treatment is quite simple and cheap and if the condition is picked up quickly woman recover well. If they have another pregnancy they can take a pill immediately after the birth and do not breast feed to prevent the condition developing. Some women have no problems with the first birth and the condition only presents after the second child.
metadata.Further information: In September 2018 the Would Health organization adopted the treatment into the International Guidelines, this generic medication and extremely cheap. This is a major success for UCT's Prof Karen Silwa who has been part of this 20 year study Shaheema Chinian was 28 years old and had a healthy 3 year old when she gave birth to her second child. She was extremely tired after her 2nd baby and she and her mother put it down to looking after two very small children. Within two months after the birth her face began to swell and she was short of breath. The local clinic treated her for asthma, but her condition did not improve. She returned to the clinic several times before going to Groote Schuur. Then suddenly her face and tongue swelled and her mother insisted she return to Groote Schuur. It took several visits before she finally told her mother that she had a heart condition. Sadly Shaheema died when her baby was just 4 months old and her first born only 3 years old. She was in her final year of law at UWC. Her death was completely preventable. Shaheema's parent are willing to be interviewed. The latest being a nursing sister who despite her medical knowledge had ver heard of this condition and she too just thought it was a result of being the mother of 3 small children. her first two pregnancies were fine.
